children: The earnings backdrop for Australian general insurers has improved rather than deteriorated since June, says Jefferies. Central banks are raising rates again. The strongest El Niño weather event on record is building in the Pacific. Reinsurance capacity remains abundant. "Against this, commercial cycles continue to soften, New Zealand remains problematic, and AI disintermediation has emerged as a new source of share price volatility," says analyst Simon Fitzgerald. Jefferies has a "buy" call on IAG, its top pick in the sector. IAG is struggling to convince regulators to approve its alliance with the Royal Automobile Club of Western Australia. Jefferies acknowledges that deal may ultimately prove challenging. Still, a material on-market share buyback by IAG would be a second-best option, it says. Jefferies has "hold" calls on Suncorp and QBE Insurance. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
